result.summary: The core hook chain works. All 13 hooks wired in ~/.claude/settings.json point at files that exist and pass a syntax check, uv, dcg, node and python3 all resolve, and the session-start, transcript-capture, skill-router, dcg and autopush hooks show recent successful runs. The main exposure is in permissions: a bare "Bash" allow rule plus auto mode with both bypass prompts turned off, and 129 allow rules, of which 20 point at Windows paths and 57 are one-off commands. The other problems are drift: plugin copies synced from the claude.ai account escape Eric's disables and quieting hooks (GitHub MCP fails with a 400 every session, and the superpowers injection still fires), the Codex copy of keystone-unified-snapshot.js is behind, a LIFEOS hooks.json with 60 entries and 50 orphan hook files is still on disk, and the skill-router roster is a month stale.

findings.title: Bare "Bash" allow rule with defaultMode auto and both permission bypass prompts suppressed
findings.evidence: ~/.claude/settings.json permissions.allow[0] = "Bash"; defaultMode "auto"; skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt true; skipAutoPermissionPrompt true; useAutoModeDuringPlan true; autoMode.allow carries a standing gh pr merge approval. 95 of the 129 allow rules are Bash(...) rules that the bare "Bash" already covers. Also allowed: Bash(launchctl:*), Bash(git:*), Bash(python:*), Bash(python3:*), Bash(node:*), Bash(npm install:*), Bash(gh api *), Bash(vercel env:*), Bash(vercel deploy:*). settings.local.json adds Bash(claude:*), Bash(npm:*) and Bash(powershell.exe:*). The only code-level Bash guard is the dcg PreToolUse hook (verified: it denies `git reset --hard`). The permission-gate hook is shadow-only and never blocks.
findings.impact: If the auto-mode classifier misses something, or a session runs in a mode that honors allow rules literally, any shell command runs without a prompt. That includes launchctl changes, global installs, git force operations and nested `claude` runs. dcg only catches its own pattern packs. I did not verify how the auto classifier treats a bare Bash rule. TypeSafe STATUS says the classifier still blocks some sends, so this is exposure, not a confirmed bypass. settings.json syncs to the Windows desktop-app sessions through dotclaude.
findings.fix: Remove the bare "Bash" rule and the broad interpreter and launchctl rules. Keep narrow read-only patterns, and leave the broad ones to the auto classifier plus dcg. Decide on purpose whether skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt is still wanted.

findings.title: Every scheduled 21:00 daily-backup since 10-14 ends in ERROR: it runs ~9h through battery sleep and its gws uploads and git pushes fail
findings.evidence: ~/.claude/scripts/logs/daily-backup.log end markers: 10-15 06:32 ERROR(7), 10-16 06:01 ERROR(7), 10-19 06:25 ERROR(7) (run started 10-17 21:09, 33h), 10-21 09:26 ERROR(7), 10-22 06:05 ERROR(5). The only OK ends are off-schedule runs (10-19 17:28, 10-22 06:53). Same uploads take seconds when awake: 10-22 nightly 'SNAP-GWS .gemini -> gemini.tgz : FAILED' at 05:19, then the 06:05 run 'gemini.tgz : OK' at 06:11:12. Timestamps jump between retries ('retrying in 5s' at 21:24:50, next attempt 21:36:34). 'Could not resolve host: github.com' on 10-17 and 10-19. `pmset -g log` 10-21 00:09-03:50 shows repeated 'Entering Sleep state ... Using Batt (Charge:38%)'. `pmset -g`: lowpowermode 1. The plist runs '/usr/bin/caffeinate -i -s'; -s only applies on AC. `launchctl print gui/501/com.keystone.dailybackup`: runs=2, last exit code=1. The 10-17 run spanning 33h swallowed the 10-18 21:00 slot (no 10-18 start line). The CRASHBOX SSD leg is skipped in every nightly run ('TARGET SSD ... NOT MOUNTED').
findings.impact: The nightly backup never completes unattended. Coverage depends on Eric re-running /backup in the morning. On days he doesn't, claude-projects, codex-sessions, gemini and launchagents snapshots and the git pushes are missed. A long sleep-stretched run also blocks the next night's run.
findings.fix: Choose one: (a) schedule the backup for a time the Mac is reliably awake and on AC (e.g. 17:00 at the desk), or (b) add `pmset repeat wakeorpoweron` and require AC (check `pmset -g batt` at start and exit early with a clear log line on battery), or (c) keep 21:00 but have reconcile replay it (see the reconcile finding). Also have the script abort when wall-clock time far exceeds the elapsed timer (a sleep was detected) instead of grinding on for 9h.
findings.known_where: Partly. ~/DEV/docs/STATUS.md 2026-10-20 notes one night's 00:05 gws uploads failed 'because the Mac was offline'. project_backup-sync-system.md says launchd catches up runs missed during sleep. findings.title: daily-backup-login.sh can start a second, concurrent backup while the 21:00 run is still going, and it treats an ERROR end as done
findings.evidence: ~/.claude/scripts/daily-backup-login.sh: `if grep -q "^$TODAY .*daily-backup end:" "$LOG"; then exit 0; fi`, then exec daily-backup.ps1. It checks for a finished run, not a running one ('shortcut: checks the log, not a lock file'). Nightly runs routinely last until 06:00-09:26 the next day (see backup finding). The pattern also matches 'end: ERROR', so a failed overnight run counts as today's backup.

findings.fix: Skip if `pgrep -f daily-backup.ps1` finds a process. Match only 'daily-backup end: OK'.

findings.title: Compile lock lets a second compile reclaim a live lock in the same second; two compiles ran at once on 10-16
findings.evidence: ~/.claude/claude-memory-compiler/scripts/compile.log lines 610-644: at 2026-10-16 23:00:07 two auto compiles started (pid 1883 and 1884). Both listed the same files (2026-10-14.md and 2026-10-16.md), their output interleaved, both wrote articles, and they reported $2.37 and $2.40 (KB went from 490 to 496). Code path: guardrails.py:132 acquire_lock opens the file with O_CREAT|O_EXCL, then writes the JSON payload in a separate step (133-134). read_lock (104-111) returns None on JSONDecodeError, which includes an empty file. acquire_lock:140-143 treats None as 'unreadable lock, treat as stale', unlinks the file and retries. A process that arrives inside the create-to-write gap therefore deletes the live lock and takes it. The code allows this, and the log shows it fired once; the race was not reproduced.
findings.impact: The same log gets compiled twice in parallel, roughly doubling spend for that run. Both processes write state.json, index.md and the article files concurrently, so the last writer wins. Article updates or ingested entries can be lost or duplicated without any error.
findings.fix: Write the payload atomically: write a temp file, then os.link or os.rename it into place under O_EXCL semantics. Or treat an empty or unparseable lock younger than a few seconds (by file mtime) as held, not stale. Only reclaim a lock with no payload when its mtime is older than STALE_LOCK_SECONDS. Add a test that runs two acquire_lock calls with the write step delayed.

result.summary: The toolchain itself is in good shape. uv is a single copy at ~/.local/bin/uv, Homebrew Python is clean, every launchd interpreter and venv exists, gh auth is valid, FileVault and SIP are on, and macOS is current. The real problem is the machine. It has 8 GB of RAM, 94% of swap is used, load is 6 to 9.5, and four Claude sessions each run their own copy of the MCP servers. The settings facts are accurate. I parsed ~/.claude/settings.json and found: allow[0]="Bash"; 129 allow rules, 96 of them Bash(...) rules; defaultMode "auto"; skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt, skipAutoPermissionPrompt and useAutoModeDuringPlan all true; no deny or ask rules; autoMode.allow carries the gh pr merge approval. Bash(launchctl:*), Bash(git:*), Bash(python:*), Bash(python3:*), Bash(node:*), Bash(npm install:*), Bash(gh api *) and Bash(vercel env:*/deploy:*) are all there. settings.local.json adds Bash(claude:*), Bash(npm:*) and Bash(powershell.exe:*). I found no earlier record of this in Tier A memory, HARNESS_FIXES.md, STORAGE.md, STATUS.md or ~/.claude/audits (the 09-30 audit lists permission-gate only as 'Not assessed').

The impact is overstated, though. I ran strings on the installed binary (~/.local/share/claude/versions/2.1.309). It has stripDangerousPermissionsForAutoMode() and the log line 'Ignoring dangerous permission ${rule} from ${source} (bypasses classifier)'. The classifier kEs() returns true for a Bash rule with no ruleContent, which is the bare "Bash". Plan-exit code calls stripDangerousPermissionsForAutoMode when it returns to auto. So with defaultMode auto, the bare Bash rule is dropped and the auto classifier still reviews commands. This matches memory: project_vendored-skill-install.md and project_drive-fuse-read-hang.md both record the classifier blocking actions. The exposure is real only in a session that runs in default or acceptEdits mode (for example after Shift-Tab, or when auto mode is unavailable and the session falls back to default). There, the bare Bash rule and the interpreter, launchctl and git wildcards do allow any command without a prompt. dcg is the only guard in that case.

skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt only skips the confirmation dialog. bypassPermissions still needs the session launched with --dangerously-skip-permissions (the binary has the string 'Cannot set permission mode to bypassPermissions because the session was not launched with --dangerously-skip-permissions'). The only unattended headless use is ~/.claude/scripts/skill-button.sh:67, which already passes --dangerously-skip-permissions, so allow rules make no difference there.

So this is a trap waiting for a mode switch plus 95+ redundant or stale rules (including Windows C:/Users/eric_rash paths), not a live bypass. That is medium.

findings.title: The herdr server runs all the time and injects session hooks into Codex and Antigravity, but is barely documented
findings.evidence: ps: '/Users/kristinarash/.local/bin/herdr server' up 2d06h; ~/.config/herdr/herdr-server.log is 505 KB, written today. ~/.codex/hooks.json SessionStart runs "bash ~/.codex/herdr-agent-state.sh session" ('managed by herdr; reinstalling... overwrites this file'). ~/.gemini/config/hooks.json has a herdr PreInvocation hook. The only documentation is one line in project_hook-two-copies-trap.md:21 and the 09-30 memory-infra audit.
findings.impact: A third-party tool owns hook files in two harnesses and rewrites them on update. That is a hidden source of hook 'reverts' (see the hook two-copies trap). Its log grows without a cap.
findings.fix: Add a short TOOLPATHS or memory note: what herdr is, which hook files it owns, how to remove it. Rotate or cap herdr-server.log.
